text:
alerts-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: route=payments-generate errors > 5% (5xx/latency). See: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/2432105678
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2432105678 — smart-routing fallback loop suspected. Paging oncall.
sofia (oncall): I'm on it. Observed spike across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 after canary rollout at 09:12 UTC. Error mix: 502 and model outputs with truncated tokens.
matt r: pinging eng-runtime and routing teams. Any recent routing policy changes?
jen p: I rolled the canary variant v2-bf-quant at 09:12 as part of staged rollout. No config changes to smart routing policy except default TTL.
sam (eng-runtime): Looking at request logs — a subset of requests are being sticky-routed to v1 (stable) due to affinity keys, but some requests then fall back to eu-west-1 and end up on v2 again because of region failover TTL mismatch. That creates an oscillation.
kai (support): Customer impact: 8 tenants reported malformed responses in the last 10m, highest impact to checkout flows (payment descriptions truncated). Marking P2 but could escalate.
sofia (oncall): Reproduced locally: when v2 short-circuits early with empty KV cache, runtime returns truncated generation (no EOS). Combination causes client retries -> region fallback -> sticky affinity keeps flipping.
matt r: Can we pause the canary rollout and force all traffic back to v1? If affinity is sticky to v2 sometimes, we need to clear sticky mappings or TTL.
sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Proposed actions:
1) pause rollout (console API)
2) set smart-routing fallback TTL=0 for 5m to break affinity rebinding
3) remove in-memory sticky entries for affected route
4) scale up v1 instances to absorb traffic if needed

jen p: Running pause now: `curl -XPOST https://console.redwood/api/rollouts/v2-bf-quant/pause -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`
ops-runner: Pause acknowledged by deploy-bot :white_check_mark:. Canary paused at 09:18 UTC.
sam (eng-runtime): Applying sticky eviction: `redis-cli -h sticky-store del route:payments-generate:*` — starting in 09:20 UTC window. I'll also set routing policy TTL to 0 via patch:
```json
{"smart_routing": {"fallback_ttl_sec": 0}}
```
sofia (oncall): Executed eviction and patch. Watching metrics.
kai (support): Notifying affected customers via status page. Draft: "We observed degraded responses on payments generation route; mitigation in progress; some customers may see retries or truncated outputs."
matt r: After eviction, I still see some requests directed to v2 from eu-west-1 for a short window. Could be cached DNS or edge sticky. Can we toggle region fallback to prefer same-region only?
sam (eng-runtime): Toggled region preference to strict-local for 2m. Also created temporary rule to route traffic for tenants with active sessions to v1: `route->override:tenant_list[...] -> variant: v1`
sofia (oncall): Error rate dropping from 6.2% -> 1.1% in last 3m. Latency back to baseline. Observability traces show fewer truncated generations.
kai (support): Customers update posted. One customer replied they still saw a bad response at 09:22 but then recovered.
matt r: Next steps: 1) keep canary paused, 2) audit sticky/affinity expiry logic in runtime (sam), 3) add rollback guard in rollout automation to ensure affinity and fallback TTL are compatible, 4) postmortem if we don't get stable in 24h.
jen p: Rolling back canary from paused state to stable is prepared: `console rollback v2-bf-quant -> v1` ready if we fail to stabilize.
sam (eng-runtime): I've opened a short-term hotfix PR to skip sticky-mapping when model variant is newly introduced in a canary for first 10m: code link https://git.internal/eng-runtime/PR/487
sofia (oncall): Summarizing incident so far for handoff to afternoon oncall: cause = affinity+fallback TTL mismatch + canary with behavioral regression; mitigation = paused canary, evicted sticky entries, strict-local region preference, temporary tenant overrides; impact = P2, ~8 tenants, transient truncated outputs and elevated 502s; status = stabilized, watching.
incident-bot: Handoff: paging next oncall @matt r in 30m for follow-up and postmortem coordination.
ops-runner: Creating incident timeline doc and assigning postmortem owner.
sofia (oncall): I'll add logs and sample requests to the incident doc, include repro steps and queries: `SELECT * FROM request_logs WHERE route='payments-generate' AND ts > 2432105600`
matt r: Thanks team. If we see reappearance after rollback unpause, escalate to SEV1. Otherwise, capture lessons: rollout must coordinate affinity semantics with routing policy changes. :memo:
